term: in potency / mutable (aliquo modo in potentia)
resolution: Q.9 a.2 distinguishes mutability through potency in the subject (DEF-POTENCY) from mutability through a power in another (DEF-MUTABLE-THROUGH-ANOTHER), such as the creator's power to withhold esse. STMT-SUCCESSION-REQUIRES-POTENCY, STMT-LIFE-BOUNDARY-REQUIRES-POTENCY, STMT-PURE-ACT-LIVES and STMT-IMMUTABLE-IS-BOETHIAN-ETERNAL all use only potency in the subject, the InPotency that PureAct quantifies over. The derivation does not pass to the wider sense: it neither shows that what lacks subject potency is unconservable nor that external dependence is excluded. The boundary premise is exactly where the wider sense would intrude: q.10 a.1 gives only that what begins is not altogether immutable. Fork (batch 4 of #1233, TruthCore.Causality.TermSenseForks4): MUTABLE_1 in the subject (DEF-POTENCY; per-use declaration MutableInSubject, ∃ r, InPotency x r), MUTABLE_2 through another (DEF-MUTABLE-THROUGH-ANOTHER, MutableThroughAnother over the typed power relation PowerOver) and MUTABLE_3 in some way (DEF-MUTABLE-IN-SOME-WAY, MutableInSomeWay, either channel; its negation is 'omnino immutabile'). The root argument IMMUTABLE-IS-PRIMITIVE-ETERNAL-FROM-TYPED-BOETHIAN uses the term twice (succession, boundary); coverage STMT-MUTABILITY-SENSES-EXHAUSTIVE and exclusivity STMT-MUTABILITY-SENSE-UNIQUE range over those uses. Per sense at the root-route node STMT-LIFE-BOUNDARY-REQUIRES-POTENCY: MUTABLE_1 is the existing LIFE-BOUNDARY-POTENCY-FROM-IMMUTABILITY; MUTABLE_2 (LIFE-BOUNDARY-POTENCY-THROUGH-ANOTHER) and MUTABLE_3 (LIFE-BOUNDARY-POTENCY-FROM-SOME-MUTABILITY) reach it only through the explicit open bridge STMT-SUBJECT-OF-ANOTHERS-POWER-HAS-POTENCY, and an omission model (a being with no potency in itself, in another's power, that begins to live) shows the bridge is needed. MUTABLE_3 is the weakest boundary reading (two strengthens relations). The mixed reading (succession MUTABLE_1, boundary MUTABLE_2) breaks MUTABILITY-SENSE-FORK-UNCHANGING-LIFE.
